questions.answer: Yes. Put new logic in review_target.py; keep flow.py and cli.py to call-site changes plus the _find_git_root fix.

description: The native Stage 4 review loop runs no reviewer: one iteration is a mergeability and CI probe, and the consensus report renders a '3-Agent Independent Ensemble' whose reviewer ids are hashed from the commit and whose votes are copies of the CI verdict (posted to GitHub on PR #97 on 2026-10-26). Stage 4 now fails closed (resolution, clone, empty diff, posting, bounded waits), but there is still no real reviewer. This change adds the reviewer ensemble itself as an isolated module: N independent reviewer agent turns, a strict report trailer parsed from each reviewer's report file, and a unanimity consensus that can never approve with zero completed reviewers.
goal:
Add the real reviewer ensemble as a new, self-contained module, built and fully tested against fakes before anything calls it. This is the second of three sequential changes: the first (already on main) made Stage 4 fail closed and added review_target.py; the third will wire this module into run_review_loop() and Stage 4 and rebuild the consensus report. Do NOT change run_review_loop(), flow.py or the consensus report in this change.
1) MODULE apps/sandbox-executor/src/sandbox_executor/review_ensemble.py with a typed, docstringed (Australian English) public API:
- ReviewerVerdict (StrEnum: APPROVED, CHANGES_REQUESTED) and ReviewerStatus (StrEnum: COMPLETED, FAILED).
- ReviewFinding dataclass (severity critical, important or nit; path; line; summary).
- ReviewerResult dataclass (index, agent, model, status, optional verdict, counts, findings, report_path, failure_reason). A FAILED result carries no verdict and is never counted as a vote.
- ReviewRequest dataclass (repo_dir, head_sha, base_ref, pr_title, pr_body, diff_text, iteration).
- parse_review_trailer(text) returning the parsed verdict, counts and findings or raising TrailerError. Trailer format: a final block delimited by '<!-- holon-review-trailer -->' and '<!-- /holon-review-trailer -->' lines containing one JSON object with keys verdict, critical, important, nit and findings (a list of objects with severity, file, line, summary); standard-library JSON only. Reject unknown verdicts, negative counts, counts that disagree with the findings list, and an APPROVED verdict with any non-zero count (unparseable, so it fails closed).
- build_reviewer_prompt(template_text, request, report_rel) filling holon-config/prompts/review_loop.template.md placeholders plus the diff, PR description and the exact report path and trailer contract.
- run_reviewer(request, index, agent, model, *, turn_runner, runner_factory, budgets, stage_timer) creating a fresh per-reviewer scratch directory under .holon/review/iter-<n>/reviewer-<i>/ (already git-ignored), building the agent command with get_runner(agent).build_cmd(...) and running it through the existing turn supervision used by the planner (supervise_authoring_turn in turns.py with an artefact spec for the report). If that supervision cannot be reused cleanly, call run_turn directly with the same TurnBudgets and StageTimer and document why; do not change turns.py beyond at most one new optional parameter. A runner exception, budget breach, missing report or TrailerError returns a FAILED result with a redacted reason. Clean ephemeral credentials in a finally, as the planner does.
- run_ensemble(request, size, agent, model, **seams) running reviewers sequentially; before each reviewer starts, earlier reviewers' report files have been read into memory and removed from the workspace, and each prompt contains only the diff and PR description, so no reviewer can see another reviewer's output.
- decide_consensus(results, configured_size, mergeable, ci_green) returning APPROVED, CHANGES_REQUESTED or FAILED: FAILED when zero reviewers were dispatched, any reviewer FAILED, or len(results) != configured_size; CHANGES_REQUESTED when any completed reviewer requested changes or reported any finding, or mergeability or CI is not clean; APPROVED only otherwise. Zero completed reviewers can never approve.
Keep every function short (about 25 lines or fewer) with at most two levels of branching and intention-revealing names.
2) PROMPT: extend holon-config/prompts/review_loop.template.md with a 'Reviewer turn contract' section: review only the supplied diff and description; write the full report to the given path; end it with the trailer block; never modify code, commit, push, call gh pr merge or enable auto-merge; never read other files under .holon/review/. Remove nothing other callers rely on.
3) TESTS (pytest only; never name any other test runner) in apps/sandbox-executor/tests/test_review_ensemble.py with a fake turn_runner that writes chosen report text, writes nothing, raises, or reports a budget breach: trailer round-trip; malformed, missing and inconsistent trailers fail; one failed reviewer blocks approval; one unparseable reviewer blocks; one CHANGES_REQUESTED blocks; a single nit blocks; zero dispatched and zero completed cannot approve; non-mergeable or red CI blocks; three clean reviewers plus mergeable and green CI approve; no reviewer's prompt contains another reviewer's report text, and earlier report files are gone when the next reviewer starts. Never touch a real runner, gh, git remote or Docker. Run the new test module first, then 'uv run task test' once; no repeated runs (not a performance change).
4) DOCS: document the module, the trailer contract and the unanimity rule where Stage 4 is described (docs/ and apps/sandbox-executor/README.md), stating that the module is not yet called by Stage 4 (the wiring is the next change).
5) CONSTRAINTS: no flow.py, cli.py or run_review_loop() changes; Australian English in comments, docstrings and log strings; no new dependencies; tests strictly via 'uv run task test' / 'uv run pytest' from the repository root (never PYTHONPATH, never from apps/sandbox-executor); 'uv run task lint' and 'uv run task lint-docs' must pass; markdown formatted with the repository configuration; keep all paths target-native (holon-knowledge/, plans/, .holon/); only the three append-only ledgers; no harness paths, bean ids or review ids in any file.

questions.question: Should the plan be split into sub-intents?
questions.answer: No. Deliver this as one plan and one execution branch; do not split it into sub-intents. It is already the second of three sequential changes.

questions.question: Should this change call the ensemble from run_review_loop() or rebuild the consensus report?
questions.answer: No. That wiring and the report rebuild are the next, separate change. This change adds and tests the module only.

questions.question: How many reviewers by default, and may approval use a majority?
questions.answer: Three by default, configurable. Approval needs unanimity: every configured reviewer completed with APPROVED and zero findings of any severity, plus mergeable and green CI.

description: The native Stage 4 review loop still decides consensus as 'not dirty and CI green' and renders a '3-Agent Independent Ensemble' report whose reviewer ids are hashed from the commit and whose votes copy the CI verdict, with a hard-coded fallback title ('Audit Remediation and Flow Review Hardening'); on PR #97 (2026-10-26) holon flow posted two such fabricated approvals of unrelated work. Stage 4 now fails closed (review_target.py) and a real reviewer ensemble exists (review_ensemble.py), but nothing calls it. This change wires the ensemble into run_review_loop() and Stage 4 so every iteration is decided by real, sandboxed reviewer results plus mergeability and CI, and the posted report contains only real reviewer data.
goal:
Wire the real reviewer ensemble into Stage 4 and remove the fabricated consensus report. This is the third and final change: the first (on main) made Stage 4 fail closed and added review_target.py; the second (on main) added review_ensemble.py (run_ensemble, decide_consensus, strict trailers, scratch-root containment), which nothing calls yet.
1) REVIEW LOOP: in run_review_loop() (call-site changes only), per iteration after the mergeability and CI probes, build a ReviewRequest from the resolved ReviewTarget, the real diff between base and head SHA, and the PR title and body; call run_ensemble() and decide_consensus(). The old rule 'not dirty and CI green' must no longer approve on its own. Record one ACT-FIND row per finding and one ACT-REV row per reviewer (agent, model, status, verdict, counts) via the existing record_review_action() under LedgerLock. Stop after the first iteration whose result is CHANGES_REQUESTED or FAILED (there is no resolver, so later iterations would review the same diff); remove the misleading per-iteration 'resolver triggered' ACT-RES row. Thread ensemble_size into run_ensemble(); reviewer agent and model come from context.agent and context.model.
2) STAGE 4 ROUTING: reviewer agent turns must run inside the sandbox, never on the host. Hypothesis: holon flow Stage 4 can dispatch the reviewer work through the existing _dispatch_role() into the existing review-loop role container, with the container running the ensemble and the host reading the outcome from the container exit code and the ledger rows it records; host-side Stage 4 keeps mergeability, CI and posting. Spend at most about 20 minutes probing this; if it does not work without a new transport, ship the fail-closed fallback instead: host-side Stage 4 refuses to dispatch reviewers outside a sandbox and fails with a clear error, and record the routing work as a follow-up in the execution notes. Either way update cli.py's _AGENT_FLOW_STAGES comment and the preflight gate so a flow resumed at review also preflights the agent runner.
3) REPORT: rewrite build_pr_review_consensus_report() to take the list of ReviewerResult objects and the real title (intent title, else the PR title from ReviewTarget; if neither, the PR number or branch only). Delete the hashlib.sha256 reviewer ids, the copied-vote loop, the 'N-Agent' wording derived from a constant and the hard-coded fallback title 'Audit Remediation and Flow Review Hardening'. Each reviewer line shows its real agent, model, status, verdict and counts; failed reviewers show as failed with their redacted reason. Move the rendering helpers out of flow.py into review_ensemble.py or, if that would exceed about 400 more lines, a sibling review_report.py. flow.py's net line count must not increase.
4) POSTING AND EXIT CODES: call post_pr_review_consensus() only when the ensemble produced at least one COMPLETED reviewer and the iteration was not FAILED for infrastructure reasons (a failed post already fails the stage). run_review_loop_cli() and the container entrypoint return 0 only for APPROVED; the summary prints the real per-reviewer verdicts. Never merge, never enable auto-merge.
5) CLI: --ensemble-size help becomes 'Number of independent reviewer agent turns per iteration; approval needs every reviewer to approve with zero findings (default: 3)'; add the same option to holon flow only if no equivalent exists (verify first); keep validation >= 1.
6) DOCS: update every current description of Stage 4 (docs/architecture.md, docs/git_flow.md, docs/agents.md, docs/budgets.md, docs/ledger_schema.md for ACT-REV/ACT-FIND rows and the removed per-iteration ACT-RES, docs/sandbox/execute_plan.md, README.md, apps/sandbox-executor/README.md): real ensemble, reviewer-count option, unanimity rule, fail-closed behaviour, and that findings stop the stage with no automatic resolver. Do not rewrite historical audit records.

description: Two defects stop sandboxed claude stages from producing work. (1) The claude runner in apps/sandbox-executor/src/sandbox_executor/agent_runner.py builds 'claude --model <m> -p [--settings ...]' with no permission bypass. In print mode Claude Code then refuses every file write, so the planner cannot write plans/P-*.md (it falls back to stdout and commits a 'permission prompt' preamble) and the executor authors nothing. The Antigravity runner already honours HOLON_AGENT_SKIP_PERMISSIONS (default true); the claude runner has no equivalent. Verified in the holon/agent-claude image: '--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions' alone only makes bypass available, and a -p write is still denied until '--permission-mode bypassPermissions' is also passed. (2) entrypoint/planner.py substitutes template placeholders with a sequence of str.replace calls and maps the partial key '{plan_id' before '{plan_id}', so 'plans/{plan_id}.md' renders as 'plans/P-...}.md' and the plan file lands under the wrong name.
goal:
1) RUNNER: the claude runner honours HOLON_AGENT_SKIP_PERMISSIONS (default true, same truthy parsing as the Antigravity runner, evaluated when the command is built, not at import) and, when enabled, emits '--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions --permission-mode bypassPermissions' as command-line parameters. The bypass must never be routed through the --settings JSON or any settings file. An explicit opt-out (HOLON_AGENT_SKIP_PERMISSIONS=false) emits neither flag. HOLON_AGENT_SETTINGS keeps mapping to --settings unchanged and coexists with the bypass flags.
2) PLACEHOLDERS: replace the planner's chained str.replace substitution with one small, intention-revealing function (for example render_placeholders(template, values)) that renders every placeholder in a single regular-expression pass, matches each placeholder in both its complete '{name}' and its unmatched '{name' form, is independent of mapping order, and inserts values literally (no re-expansion of braces or backslashes inside values). Use it for every planner template substitution.
3) TESTS (pytest only; never name any other test runner): runner default-on emits both flags; explicit opt-out emits neither; flag ordering yields a valid claude command line; coexistence with HOLON_AGENT_SETTINGS; the bypass never appears inside the --settings value. Placeholders: plans/{plan_id}.md renders correctly; an unmatched '{plan_id' renders; order independence; literal values containing braces and backslashes. Add a test that loads every shipped holon-config/prompts/*.template.md and fails if any contains an unmatched placeholder brace. Tests must never call real Docker, git remotes, gh or LLM runners.
4) CONSTRAINTS: Australian English in comments, docstrings and log strings; no new dependencies; keep functions short and low in branching; tests strictly via 'uv run task test' / 'uv run pytest' from the repository root (never PYTHONPATH); 'uv run task lint' and 'uv run task lint-docs' must pass; keep all paths target-native; never create auxiliary ledgers and keep the three ledgers append-only; update any docs that describe the claude runner's flags or HOLON_AGENT_SKIP_PERMISSIONS.

questions.question: May the bypass be passed through the --settings JSON instead of CLI parameters?
questions.answer: No. The maintainer's decision is CLI parameters only: '--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions --permission-mode bypassPermissions'.

questions.question: Should the bypass be on by default?
questions.answer: Yes, matching the Antigravity runner: HOLON_AGENT_SKIP_PERMISSIONS defaults to true, and an explicit false opts out. Sandboxed role containers are the only place the claude runner executes.

questions.question: Is this one intent or should it split?
questions.answer: One intent. Both fixes are small, independent and needed together for a sandboxed claude stage to write its outputs under the correct names.

description: Stage 3 silently discards the executor agent's code whenever the execution fails. In apps/sandbox-executor/src/sandbox_executor/entrypoint/executor.py the failure path stages only holon-knowledge/ledger/executions.jsonl and the notes file (:1820-1826), and 'git add -A' runs only when exec_status == "success" (:1828); the comment at :1789 says it outright: 'Salvage commits (ledger + partial notes, never code)'. docs/budgets.md:167-170 documents the same ('stages the partial notes, but not the code changes'). The workspace lives inside a --rm container, so everything unstaged is lost when it exits. Real occurrence on 2026-10-27: a Stage 3 run used 44.1 of its 43.9-minute budget after editing 14 files (tests, a workflow, pyproject.toml, uv.lock, two docs) and recording three plan steps as complete; its failure commit contained only the notes and the ledger row, so the pushed execution branch describes work that does not exist on it. Three related gaps: (a) the push at :1939 is a run_cmd with the default check, so a refused push exits the entrypoint and the local commit dies with the container; (b) the repo-local git identity is configured only just before the final commit (:1840) and in the pre-push sync (:1015), so an agent cannot commit its own work step by step inside the container; (c) a resumed flow cannot continue from partial work: flow.py's Stage 3 always dispatches the executor with [plan_branch, agent, model] (:2998) and the executor always cuts the new execution branch from the plan branch tip (executor.py:1315-1323).
goal:
1) SALVAGE: on every Stage 3 failure that reaches the commit step (a budget breach, an agent exit other than 0, an unusable notes file or any other non-success status), stage all of the agent's working-tree changes (tracked modifications and deletions, and untracked files that .gitignore does not exclude) and commit them on the execution branch in a commit of their own, titled 'execute: <execution id> partial work (failed) for plan <plan branch>', ahead of the existing failure commit for the notes and the ledger row. The failure summary row in executions.jsonl keeps status 'failure' and gains an optional 'partial_head' field holding that commit's sha (absent when there was nothing to salvage and on success). Code is never silently dropped. The existing pre-push safety and sync checks apply unchanged, and the successful path is unchanged.
2) IDENTITY: configure the repo-local executor git identity immediately after the execution branch is created and before the agent runs, so commits the agent makes step by step land on the execution branch and survive a later failure. The entrypoint never squashes, amends or rewrites the agent's commits.
3) REJECTED PUSH: a refused 'git push' of the execution branch (success or failure) must not end the entrypoint through an unhandled exit that loses the commits. Catch it, print a redacted error naming the branch, the local head sha and git's reason, then print the work as a redacted 'git format-patch --stdout <plan tip>..HEAD' between explicit 'BEGIN UNPUSHED EXECUTION PATCH' / 'END UNPUSHED EXECUTION PATCH' marker lines on stderr, so the host's captured log keeps a recoverable copy without any new container mount. Cap the block at a named size constant; above it print 'git diff --stat <plan tip>..HEAD' and say the patch was omitted. Then exit non-zero. Do not add token-scope checks or a pre-flight gate; that is separate work.
4) RESUME: when 'holon flow' resumes at Stage 3 (a --checkpoint or --from-stage execute resume) and origin holds a failed execution branch under the same plan whose latest summary row carries a partial_head, flow.py passes that execution branch as an extra fourth positional executor argument through the existing _dispatch_role call (no cli.py change; the positional list is already forwarded to the container). The executor verifies that the partial head descends from the plan branch tip, cuts the new execution branch from the partial head instead of the plan tip, and tells the agent in code (by appending a short continuation note to the rendered prompt, not by editing any prompt template) that it is continuing partial work. The empty-diff guard still compares against the plan tip. If no partial head exists, or it does not descend from the plan tip, the executor starts from the plan tip and logs why. A plain 'holon execute <plan_branch>' and a non-resumed flow keep starting from the plan tip.
5) DOCS: in docs/budgets.md only, replace the 'stages the partial notes, but not the code changes' description with the new behaviour: the partial-work commit and its title, the partial_head field, the unpushed-patch block and how to apply it, and the resume semantics. Document partial_head there because docs/ledger_schema.md belongs to a concurrent change.
6) TESTS (pytest only, never real Docker, git remotes, gh or LLM runners; local bare repositories under tmp_path are fine): in tests/test_executor.py, a budget breach with dirty tracked and untracked files leaves them in a partial-work commit on the execution branch and the summary row has status 'failure' with partial_head equal to that commit; the same for an agent exit other than 0; gitignored files are not committed; nothing-to-salvage records no partial_head; the success path still produces one completed commit; the identity is configured before the agent is dispatched; a refused push exits non-zero and prints the markers and the patch, and a fake token value placed in the diff never appears unredacted; an oversized patch falls back to the diffstat. In tests/test_flow.py, a Stage 3 resume with a failed branch carrying partial_head dispatches four positional arguments, and without one dispatches three.
7) CONSTRAINTS: Australian English in comments, docstrings, docs and log strings; no new dependencies unless this intent explicitly requires one (it does not); keep functions short and low in branching; tests strictly via 'uv run task test' / 'uv run pytest' from the repository root (never PYTHONPATH, never name any other test runner); 'uv run task lint' and 'uv run task lint-docs' must pass; keep all paths target-native (never reference harness directories such as .beans/, todo/, .agents/, bean ids or review ids in any target file this change writes); never create auxiliary ledgers and keep the three ledgers under holon-knowledge/ledger/ append-only. TOUCH SET: this change may modify only apps/sandbox-executor/src/sandbox_executor/entrypoint/executor.py, apps/sandbox-executor/src/sandbox_executor/flow.py, apps/sandbox-executor/tests/test_executor.py, apps/sandbox-executor/tests/test_flow.py and docs/budgets.md (in particular holon-config/prompts/, apps/sandbox-executor/src/sandbox_executor/cli.py, docs/ledger_schema.md, docs/git_flow.md and README.md are off-limits), plus the flow's own append-only ledger rows and its plans/ and executions/ records; every other file is off-limits because concurrent changes own them, and a step that seems to need another file must be dropped and reported in the execution notes instead.

questions.answer: One intent. Salvage, identity, rejected-push preservation and resume are one guarantee (an execution's code is never lost) and share the executor commit path; splitting them would make concurrent edits to the same lines.

questions.answer: No. A concurrent change owns holon-config/prompts/ and adds that instruction. This change only makes such commits possible (identity before the agent runs) and keeps them on failure.

questions.answer: Implement it, for flow resumes at Stage 3 only, through the existing positional-argument dispatch so cli.py is not touched. A plain 'holon execute' keeps restarting from the plan.

questions.answer: In docs/budgets.md only. docs/ledger_schema.md and docs/git_flow.md belong to a concurrent change; a later change can cross-reference it there.

questions.question: Is a token-scope pre-flight for rejected pushes part of this change?
questions.answer: No. This change only preserves and reports the work when a push is refused; detecting missing scopes before Stage 3 is separate work.

description: The in-container planner and executor are never told when repeated test runs are justified or how to run them, and the executor is never told to commit as it goes. holon-config/prompts/executor.template.md:10-11 says only 'Run the relevant test suite (e.g., `pytest` or `.venv/bin/pytest`)': a bare runner, no pytest-xdist, no affected-tests-first order and no limit on repetition. Neither holon-config/prompts/planner.template.md nor executor.template.md mentions xdist, worksteal or repeated runs at all. The executor's Write Protocol (executor.template.md:17-25) covers the notes file only and never asks the agent to commit completed steps, so a budget breach late in a long plan loses every step. docs/testing/testing_guide.md:47-52 documents the xdist run but has no rule on repetition. Real cost: one Stage 3 attempt took 75.7 minutes, about 55 of them on test runs, 27 of those on 50 serial runs of two test files under CPU load (about 30 s each); under '-n auto' the same files ran in 16.97 s.
goal:
1) PLANNER (holon-config/prompts/planner.template.md): add a short rule, in target-native wording: plan repeated test runs only when the intent requires measuring performance or timing behaviour (test-suite speed, a timing-sensitive or flaky test, a stated performance target); otherwise plan the affected tests first and then one full 'uv run task test'. When repetition is required, take N from the intent, or state N and the reason in the plan; never open-ended or 'many' runs. Add a commit-as-you-go directive: after each completed plan step, stage and commit the work on the current branch with a short message naming the step; never push, rebase, amend, squash or switch branches (the entrypoint pushes and records the execution).
3) DOCS: add the rule to docs/testing/testing_guide.md next to the existing xdist section (:47-52), including when repetition is justified, the explicit N, the worksteal flag and the reporting of each run and the median.
4) TESTS (pytest only) in apps/sandbox-executor/tests/test_prompt_templates.py: render the shipped planner and executor templates with the repository's own placeholder renderer and assert the rendered text contains the performance-only condition, the explicit-N requirement, '-n auto --dist worksteal' and the median reporting; the executor text names 'uv run task test', no longer contains '.venv/bin/pytest', and contains the commit-per-step directive together with the never-push instruction. The existing unmatched-placeholder test must keep passing, so the new prose must contain no curly braces.
5) CONSTRAINTS: Australian English in comments, docstrings, docs and log strings; no new dependencies unless this intent explicitly requires one (it does not); keep functions short and low in branching; tests strictly via 'uv run task test' / 'uv run pytest' from the repository root (never PYTHONPATH, never name any other test runner); 'uv run task lint' and 'uv run task lint-docs' must pass; keep all paths target-native (never reference harness directories such as .beans/, todo/, .agents/, bean ids or review ids in any target file this change writes); never create auxiliary ledgers and keep the three ledgers under holon-knowledge/ledger/ append-only. description: test_every_delimiter_in_a_password_stays_off_argv_and_echo in apps/sandbox-executor/tests/test_url_message_fuzz.py fails intermittently with false leaks. _leaks (:283-286) reports a leak when any FRAGMENT_LEN = 4 (:32) character substring of a fake password part occurs anywhere in the haystack, and the parts are 12 random letters from secrets.choice (_letters, :49-50, used at :371). The 'main-argv' and 'echo' texts (:418-420) include the docker --env-file path, which lives under pytest's tmp directory (for example '.../pytest-of-runner/pytest-0/...') and carries a random temp-file suffix. description: The entropy and Expected Value (EV) model that drives every flow decision is documented only formula-first. docs/metrics.md opens (:1-30) with bootstrap-metric goals and then 'Core Definitions: Config-Driven Physics' (λ, μ, w_i, u_i, α..ε coefficients) and continues with weighted sums and coefficient tables over 600 lines; holon-config/metrics/README.md is formula-first as well. Nothing explains in everyday language what entropy and EV mean here, how they relate, or what the entropy budget does, so a reader without the maths cannot follow why a plan is accepted, refused or split. Primary sources the explainer must agree with: holon-config/metrics/ev_config.json (lambda 0.3, mu 0.5); holon-config/metrics/entropy_config.json (w1_ssa 0.30, w2_irr 0.25, w3_cl 0.20, w4_ser 0.15, w5_nov 0.10, with its note that these weights are reserved and not yet loaded by the runtime); DEFAULT_ENTROPY_BUDGET = 15.0 in apps/sandbox-executor/src/sandbox_executor/budgets.py:313; the planner template's sub-intent rule (holon-config/prompts/planner.template.md:41-45); and EV = P(success) * Impact + mu * LearningValue - lambda * entropy - Cost.
goal:
1) Add a plain-language explainer, either as a new lead-in section at the top of docs/metrics.md or as docs/metrics-explained.md linked from the top of docs/metrics.md (the planner decides). It explains in everyday English: (a) what entropy means here: a score for how much mess and risk a change creates, built from how much code it touches (State Surface Area), how hard it is to undo (Irreversibility), how likely it collides with other work (Conflict Likelihood), how likely it breaks out of its safety sandbox (Sandbox Escape Risk) and how unfamiliar the territory is (Novelty); (b) what EV means here: whether a plan is worth doing, from its chance of success and the good it does, plus what is learnt, minus the mess (entropy) and the cost; (c) how they relate: entropy sits inside EV as a penalty, so the aim is the most value for the least mess, not zero mess, and valuable but messy work is split into smaller pieces instead of being abandoned; (d) what the entropy budget does: each intent carries a mess allowance (entropy_budget, default 15.0), and a plan predicted to exceed it must list sub-intents before it can execute.
2) One worked example with real numbers from this repository's own ledger, identified only by its plan id: plan P-1793223729-claude-agent-claude-opus-5-5 in holon-knowledge/ledger/plans.jsonl (p_success 0.7, impact 90.0, learning_value 6.0, entropy 10.6, cost 21.5, entropy_budget 14.0, ev 41.32), worked through in arithmetic: 0.7 x 90 = 63; 0.5 x 6 = 3; 0.3 x 10.6 = 3.18; 63 + 3 - 3.18 - 21.5 = 41.32, within its budget of 14.0. Do not identify the example in any other way.
3) Analogies are welcome (for example building LEGO in a shared room), but every analogy is followed by the precise sentence it stands for. No LaTeX in the plain-language part; the EV formula appears once in words and once in symbols in code spans. A reader with a high-school education and arithmetic only must be able to answer, after one read: what is entropy here, what is EV, and why does high entropy lower EV?
4) Keep the existing formal reference intact and cross-link both ways between the explainer and the formal sections. Do not overstate the runtime: say plainly that the entropy weights are documented but not yet loaded by the runtime.
5) This is documentation only: no behaviour, config or test change.
6) CONSTRAINTS: Australian English in comments, docstrings, docs and log strings; no new dependencies unless this intent explicitly requires one (it does not); keep functions short and low in branching; tests strictly via 'uv run task test' / 'uv run pytest' from the repository root (never PYTHONPATH, never name any other test runner); 'uv run task lint' and 'uv run task lint-docs' must pass; keep all paths target-native (never reference harness directories such as .beans/, todo/, .agents/, bean ids or review ids in any target file this change writes); never create auxiliary ledgers and keep the three ledgers under holon-knowledge/ledger/ append-only. TOUCH SET: this change may modify only docs/metrics.md and, if the planner chooses the separate-page option, one new file docs/metrics-explained.md (in particular README.md, holon-config/metrics/ and every other doc are off-limits), plus the flow's own append-only ledger rows and its plans/ and executions/ records; every other file is off-limits because concurrent changes own them, and a step that seems to need another file must be dropped and reported in the execution notes instead.

description: Nothing stops a change that makes CI slower from reaching main: no workflow under .github/workflows/ (build-images, make, test-hygiene, test-integration, test-stress, test-unit) records or compares job durations, and test-unit.yml's only test command (its last line) produces no per-test timing report. A real slow-down already happened: unit (macos-latest) on main rose from 160-218 s (2026-10-24) to 682 s at e3bbd67 and 609 s at e0dfd24 (run 40468502785), and came back to 131-223 s only after an unrelated parallelism fix, with nothing failing in between. Calibration data (job wall clock, started_at to completed_at, from the GitHub API) for the 13 successful main pushes of 2026-10-24 to 2026-10-29: latest main cc4bf1b gives unit 132 s ubuntu / 131 s macOS (run 40812897144), integration 153 s (run 40812897170), Workspace survival stress 263 s (run 40812897147), hygiene 28 s (run 40812897162) and make build 5 s ubuntu / 10 s macOS (run 40812897238). Ranges over the window: unit ubuntu 86-432 s, unit macOS 131-682 s, integration 131-178 s, stress 85-430 s, hygiene 21-46 s, make 4-12 s; build-images.yml is manual-dispatch only and has no runs. Replaying a rolling median of the previous 5 runs over this series, a 50 % tolerance combined with a 120 s minimum absolute delta flags exactly four historical runs: the unit slow-down at e0dfd24 (432 s vs 256 s ubuntu, 609 s vs 218 s macOS, run 40468502785), a stress spike at fbd3b35 (430 s vs 137 s, run 40501662572) and the lasting stress step at acb5dc0 (278 s vs 156 s, run 40714173246). The four most recent main runs (b1b5a1b, f09ca5e, e187393, cc4bf1b) all pass. A 25 % / 30 s setting flagged six runs, including healthy noise. Hosted-runner noise is large (hygiene alone ranged 21-46 s), which is why a minimum absolute delta is needed.
goal:
1) RECORD: on every successful push to main, each CI job (every job in every workflow under .github/workflows/, including the image-build jobs) records its wall-clock duration (from a timestamp taken in the job's first step to the gate step at its end), the job name and the runner OS; test jobs also record pytest's per-test durations through a '--junitxml=<path>' flag added to the test command in the workflow file (not in pyproject.toml or the Makefile). Store the record as a workflow artefact named per job and OS, never in the repository and never as a ledger.
2) COMPARE: on a pull request each job compares its duration with the rolling median of the last N successful main records for the same job and OS, fetched read-only with the workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN (grant 'actions: read' only where it is needed). While fewer than N records exist (cold start, or a job that has never run on main) the relative check is skipped with an explicit notice and only the ceiling applies.
3) FAIL: the job fails only when its duration exceeds the baseline median by more than the relative tolerance AND by more than the minimum absolute delta. Defaults, calibrated from the real runs cited in the description: N = 5, tolerance = 50 %, minimum absolute delta = 120 s.
4) EXPLAIN: test jobs compare per-test times with the baseline median and name the top 10 tests whose time grew by more than 50 % and more than 5 s; this report is printed on every pull-request run and appended to the failure message, and does not fail the job on its own.
5) CEILING: every job also fails above an absolute ceiling of 600 s, whatever the baseline. 600 s passes every job on today's main (the largest of the last six main runs of any job is 278 s; the largest in the whole window is 430 s) and would have failed the 682 s unit run.
6) OVERRIDE: a pull-request label 'timing-regression-accepted' turns a relative-check failure into a printed warning that names the label, so every override is visible on the pull request. The ceiling cannot be overridden by label; it changes only through a committed edit to its flag in the workflow file.
7) CONFIGURATION: N, the tolerance, the minimum delta and the ceiling are command-line flags of the script, set in the workflow commands, never in pyproject.toml or the Makefile.
8) SCRIPT AND TESTS: a single new module scripts/ci_timing_gate.py (standard library only; network and artefact access behind small injectable functions) and apps/sandbox-executor/tests/test_ci_timing_gate.py (pytest only, with fake fetchers; never real network, gh or GitHub API calls). Cover: rolling median; pass inside the tolerance; fail only when both the tolerance and the minimum delta are exceeded; the ceiling; cold start below N; label override of the relative check but not the ceiling; the per-test top-offender report; JUnit parsing; and a replay of the real durations cited in the description showing that the most recent main runs pass.
9) DOCS: document the gate, its defaults and why they were chosen, how to read the report and how to accept a deliberate slow-down in .github/workflows/README.md.
10) Pushing workflow-file changes requires a token with the 'workflow' scope; if the execution branch push is refused for that reason, report it as a blocker rather than dropping the workflow edits.
11) CONSTRAINTS: Australian English in comments, docstrings, docs and log strings; no new dependencies unless this intent explicitly requires one (it does not); keep functions short and low in branching; tests strictly via 'uv run task test' / 'uv run pytest' from the repository root (never PYTHONPATH, never name any other test runner); 'uv run task lint' and 'uv run task lint-docs' must pass; keep all paths target-native (never reference harness directories such as .beans/, todo/, .agents/, bean ids or review ids in any target file this change writes); never create auxiliary ledgers and keep the three ledgers under holon-knowledge/ledger/ append-only. TOUCH SET: this change may modify only .github/workflows/*.yml, .github/workflows/README.md, the new scripts/ci_timing_gate.py and the new apps/sandbox-executor/tests/test_ci_timing_gate.py (in particular pyproject.toml, the Makefile, uv.lock and all source under apps/ are off-limits), plus the flow's own append-only ledger rows and its plans/ and executions/ records; every other file is off-limits because concurrent changes own them, and a step that seems to need another file must be dropped and reported in the execution notes instead.

questions.answer: Measured on real main runs: single-run comparison and tight tolerances flag healthy runner noise, while 50 % plus 120 s over a rolling median of 5 flags only the real unit slow-down and the stress spike and step, and passes the four most recent main runs. description: Make the flow's posted Stage 4 review a single short consensus comment rendered from real reviewer data. rationale: Two attempts under this contract have already failed and neither is mergeable as it stands. The first rewrote the review prompt into a 16-role persona registry with its own output schema, printed five fixed Verified assertions on every approval regardless of what reviewers checked, coerced the APPROVED heading from a boolean, dropped the finding id and recommendation columns, and never built the reviewer-to-report seam - so the generator had no real data to render. Merging remains with the human maintainer.'
Roles the diff never triggered are absent from the role table rather than reported as PASS, and a finding raised by several reviewers appears once with the contributors named in the Finding cell.
Every '**Verified:**' bullet names a file, module or test that evidences it. The five fixed assertions are deleted, and no approval may assert anything the reviewer data does not carry.

The verdict heading follows the ensemble verdict alone: the promotion of a non-verdict to APPROVED when an approved flag is set is removed, and an unmeasured mergeability or CI probe renders as unmeasured instead of clean.

description: Make the flow engine the sole owner of the Stage 4 review loop: the engine owns the iteration counter, the iteration budget and the checkpointed count, and dispatches the containerised review-loop entrypoint for exactly ONE ensemble pass per engine iteration. Today _dispatch_review_ensemble passes the engine's current iteration number as the container's loop limit (--max-iterations={iteration}), so on a resumed engine iteration N a fresh container may loop N times internally over one head; the two counters mean different things and the engine's counter silently changes the container's behaviour.
goal: One loop, the engine's. 1) SINGLE-SHOT DISPATCH: the engine always dispatches the review container for exactly one ensemble pass per engine iteration, and passes the engine's iteration number through a separate labelling flag (for example --iteration=N) used only for the ledger's review_iteration fields and the posted 'Iteration {n}' heading - never as the container's loop limit. 2) STANDALONE LOOP PRESERVED: the review-loop entrypoint's internal multi-iteration loop remains only for standalone review invocations (the review CLI command); its --max-iterations flag keeps its meaning there and is never derived from another component's counter. 3) ENGINE BUDGETS: the engine's iteration budget and per-iteration time budget stay the sole caps for Stage 4, persisted in the flow checkpoint so a --from-stage review resume continues the engine count instead of restarting it, and the next dispatch after a resume carries the continued iteration number in its label. 4) TESTS (pytest only, never name another test runner; no real Docker, gh, git remotes or LLM calls): the dispatch requests exactly one pass regardless of the engine iteration number; the labelling iteration number flows into the ledger entries and the posted review body; a resumed review continues the engine count; the standalone review command's own loop behaviour is unchanged. 5) CONSTRAINTS: Australian English; no new dependencies; keep functions short and low in branching; tests strictly via 'uv run task test' / 'uv run pytest' from the repository root (never PYTHONPATH); 'uv run task lint' and 'uv run task lint-docs' must pass; keep all paths target-native; keep exactly the three append-only ledgers. TOUCH SET: only the files listed in this intent's scope array, plus plans/, executions/ and the three ledgers.
rationale: Observed during a manual end-to-end flow run: Stage 4 dispatched the container with --max-iterations=1, which puzzled the operator because the value is not a configured cap but the engine's own loop counter reused as the container's limit. The engine already owns a 25-iteration loop with per-iteration budgets and a checkpoint; the container's internal loop exists for standalone use. Reusing one counter as the other's limit couples them incorrectly: a resumed engine iteration N would permit N internal passes over a single head. Separating 'which pass is this' (a label) from 'how many passes may you run' (always one, under the engine) makes Stage 4's behaviour predictable and keeps the standalone command intact. This also prepares Stage 4 for an in-loop resolver step, where the engine's iteration structure must be the only loop.
acceptance_criteria: The engine's Stage 4 dispatch never passes its iteration counter as the container's loop limit; every dispatch requests exactly one ensemble pass.
The container receives the engine's iteration number through a dedicated labelling flag and uses it only for ledger review_iteration fields and the posted 'Iteration {n}' heading.
The standalone review CLI command's internal multi-iteration loop and its --max-iterations flag behave exactly as before.
A --from-stage review resume continues the engine's checkpointed iteration count and labels the next dispatch accordingly.
All listed tests pass via 'uv run pytest'; 'uv run task lint' and 'uv run task lint-docs' pass.

questions.question: Should the container's internal multi-iteration loop be removed entirely?
questions.answer: No. It remains for standalone review invocations; the engine simply stops using it as its own cap and always requests a single pass.

questions.question: May the labelling flag reuse the existing --max-iterations flag with a value of 1?
questions.answer: No. The label and the limit must be separate flags so the iteration number can rise across resumes while the per-dispatch pass count stays one.

description: Put resolution inside the flow engine's Stage 4 review loop so it converges instead of halting at the first CHANGES_REQUESTED verdict. Today the engine reviews once, records the findings, posts the consensus and fails the stage ('no automatic resolver; findings stop the stage'), leaving its multi-iteration loop machinery unused because nothing inside the flow ever changes the head between passes. A loop that only reviews is a reviewer, not a loop.
goal: Stage 4 is review AND resolve, iterating to convergence inside the flow. 1) RESOLVER PASS: when an engine iteration's ensemble verdict is CHANGES_REQUESTED, dispatch a resolver role container (same dispatch machinery as the reviewer, fresh clone of the execution branch) that receives that iteration's findings (ids, severities, file:line, summaries, recommendations) through the engine's result-file transport; it adjudicates EVERY finding, nits included, to exactly one disposition - applied (fixed, committed to the execution branch with the finding ids in the commit message, pushed) or rejected (with a one-line reason: not diff-grounded, inaccurate, out of scope, or conflicting with a higher-severity finding) - runs the repository's lint and test tasks before pushing, and never force-pushes or rewrites history. 2) ITERATE: after a resolver push the next engine iteration reviews the new head; any push invalidates earlier votes, so a new head is always re-reviewed in full. Exits: consensus approval (posted once, stage succeeds) or the engine's iteration/time budgets (stage fails with every finding and disposition recorded). No human pause mid-loop; the consensus is posted only at an exit, never per intermediate iteration. 3) LEDGER: the resolver's action entries populate the existing review_disposition, rejection_reason, review_finding_ids and introduced_by_action_id fields in the execution ledger; rejected findings carry their reason and are passed to the next iteration's reviewers as already adjudicated so they are not re-raised. 4) CONVERGENCE GUARDS: a finding set that survives unchanged across 3 consecutive iterations with no diff change is adjudicated rejected with reason no-convergence and reported rather than spun on. 5) TESTS (pytest only, never name another test runner; no real Docker, gh, git remotes or LLM calls): review-with-findings dispatches the resolver; every finding ends with a disposition; rejected findings are not re-raised by the next iteration; the 3-iteration no-convergence guard; approval exits post exactly once; budget exhaustion records open findings and dispositions. 6) ITERATION FLAG DOCUMENTATION: extend the review-loop entrypoint's --iteration help text (and any doc that describes it) to state the resume semantics explicitly: the engine owns the counter, saves it in the flow checkpoint, and on a resume from the review stage passes the CONTINUED count as this label, so ledger review_iteration values and posted 'Iteration {n}' headings form one monotonic sequence across halts and resumes; it is never a loop limit and is never set by operators. 7) CONSTRAINTS: Australian English; no new dependencies; keep functions short and low in branching; tests strictly via 'uv run task test' / 'uv run pytest' from the repository root (never PYTHONPATH); 'uv run task lint' and 'uv run task lint-docs' must pass; keep all paths target-native; keep exactly the three append-only ledgers; merging stays with the human maintainer. TOUCH SET: only the files listed in this intent's scope array, plus plans/, executions/ and the three ledgers.
rationale: The engine's Stage 4 already owns the iteration counter, budgets and checkpoint, and dispatches single-shot review containers with an iteration label. The halt-on-findings design made sense while nothing could change the head inside the flow, but it forces every findings-bearing run through a manual external resolution and resume, and it leaves the engine's 25-iteration budget as dead machinery. Adding a resolver step inside the engine iteration - review, resolve, push, re-review - completes the loop while preserving every existing safety property: fail-closed budgets, append-only ledger provenance for every disposition, posting only at exits, and human-only merging.
acceptance_criteria: An engine iteration whose ensemble verdict is CHANGES_REQUESTED dispatches a resolver container with that iteration's findings; the next iteration reviews the pushed head.
Every finding, nits included, ends with exactly one recorded disposition (applied or rejected with a one-line reason) in the execution ledger's existing disposition fields.
Rejected findings are handed to the next iteration's reviewers as already adjudicated and are not re-raised.
A finding set unchanged across 3 consecutive iterations with no diff change is adjudicated rejected: no-convergence and the loop proceeds to its exit.
The consensus is posted exactly once, at an exit (approval or budget exhaustion), never per intermediate iteration.
The resolver never force-pushes, never rewrites history, and runs lint and tests before each push.
All listed tests pass via 'uv run pytest'; 'uv run task lint' and 'uv run task lint-docs' pass.
The --iteration flag's help text documents the checkpoint-continued resume semantics (engine-owned label, monotonic across resumes, never a loop limit, never operator-set).

questions.question: Should the resolver be a new role container or reuse the review-loop entrypoint with a mode flag?
questions.answer: Either is acceptable; prefer whichever keeps functions short and reuses the existing dispatch and result-file transport. It must be a fresh clone of the execution branch per dispatch.

questions.question: Does the intermediate consensus still get dual-posted to the change request thread each iteration?
questions.answer: No. Posting happens exactly once, at an exit: the final approval, or the budget-exhaustion summary with open findings and dispositions.

description: Make GitHub CI a post-review gate in Stage 4 run_review_loop() rather than waiting for CI registration and pending CI checks before launching the reviewer ensemble. Reviewers must launch immediately while CI runs in parallel, and pending CI checks should only be waited on when all reviewers approve with zero open findings.
goal: 1) IMMEDIATE REVIEWER LAUNCH: In apps/sandbox-executor/src/sandbox_executor/flow.py (run_review_loop), launch the reviewer ensemble immediately after the empty-diff guard, PR creation/update, and mergeability check — do NOT block on _wait_for_ci_registration() or _wait_for_pending_ci() before dispatching reviewers. 2) FAST PATH ON REVIEWER FINDINGS: If reviewers report any open findings (CHANGES_REQUESTED), probe CI once without waiting on pending checks: if any check has already failed (failed > 0), include FIND-CI-{iteration:03d} alongside reviewer findings; if checks are merely pending (pending > 0 and failed == 0), do NOT wait on pending CI and do NOT add FIND-CI-{iteration:03d} — hand the reviewer findings straight to the resolver so it can fix and push immediately. 3) POST-REVIEW CI GATE ON CLEAN REVIEW: Only when all reviewers return APPROVED with zero open findings (and mergeability is clean), run _wait_for_ci_registration() (if needed) and _wait_for_pending_ci() to wait for pending CI checks to settle before calling decide_consensus(). If CI settles green, approve and exit; if CI fails or times out pending, record FIND-CI-{iteration:03d} and dispatch the resolver. 4) TESTS: Update and add hermetic unit tests in apps/sandbox-executor/tests/test_flow.py and apps/sandbox-executor/tests/test_review_loop.py verifying: (a) when reviewers return findings while CI is pending, zero CI wait sleep occurs and the resolver runs immediately without FIND-CI; (b) when reviewers return clean while CI is pending, the loop waits for CI to settle and approves once green (or dispatches resolver with FIND-CI if CI fails). 5) CONSTRAINTS: Australian English; no new dependencies; tests strictly via 'uv run pytest'; 'uv run task lint' and 'uv run task lint-docs' pass; keep all paths target-native; keep the three append-only ledgers; merging stays with the human maintainer.
rationale: Waiting 5-10 minutes for GitHub Actions CI to finish before starting code review wastes wall-clock time whenever reviewers find issues, because the resolver's subsequent push immediately supersedes that CI run. Launching reviewers immediately lets GitHub CI run in parallel with the LLM review pass and treats CI strictly as a gate before approval.
acceptance_criteria: run_review_loop dispatches reviewers before waiting on CI registration or pending CI checks.
When reviewers return findings while CI is pending (failed == 0), _wait_for_pending_ci is not called and the resolver is invoked immediately.
When reviewers return unanimous APPROVED with zero findings while CI is pending, _wait_for_pending_ci waits for CI to settle before finalising consensus.
All unit tests in apps/sandbox-executor pass via 'uv run pytest'.

description: Enable the Stage 4 review loop resolver to fix GitHub Actions CI and test failures by synthesizing a first-class FindingRow for FIND-CI whenever CI or test suites fail, even when all ensemble reviewers approve.

1. description: The Stage 4 resolver's pre-push verification (_verify_before_push in entrypoint/review_loop.py) runs 'uv run task lint' and 'uv run task test', but no agent image ships uv. When the resolver agent does not install uv itself, the resolver crashes with FileNotFoundError: 'uv', its fixes are lost, the loop starts the next iteration as if the findings were resolved, and the consensus post can claim a unanimous approval with zero findings that the final iteration did not record. Ship uv in the images, make missing verification tooling a loud, structured failure, and make the consensus post report the final iteration's real verdicts.
goal: 1) SHIP UV: Install a pinned uv release in the holon-base stage of apps/sandbox-executor/Dockerfile so that every image built from it (all agent images and the orchestrator) has uv on PATH for the holon user. Pin it via a single build argument or constant, and use the existing cache-mount pattern where one fits. Add a build-time smoke check (uv --version) so that an image without uv fails to build. Update apps/sandbox-executor/docs/docker_bake.md if it lists image contents. 2) FAIL LOUDLY: In entrypoint/review_loop.py, make _verify_before_push (and run_cmd as it uses it) catch a missing executable (FileNotFoundError or OSError from subprocess) and return a structured verification failure, with an actionable message naming the missing tool, instead of raising. _commit_and_push_resolution and _run_resolver_mode must report this as a resolver failure in the resolver result: no commit, no push, and the error preserved. The flow's review loop (sandbox_executor.flow.review package) must halt the loop with that error. It must never start the next iteration as if the findings had been applied. A resolver container that exits non-zero, or produces no result, must likewise halt the loop with its exit code and the tail of its output, instead of being treated as a pass with no changes. 3) HONEST CONSENSUS POST: The consensus review posted to GitHub (review_report.py and the flow's review_post module) must render the per-reviewer verdicts and the critical, important and nit counts of the final iteration exactly as recorded. The approval fraction in the heading (for example 2/3 against 3/3) must match the number of reviewers who actually approved. Open findings that remain in the final iteration must be listed, never reported as zero. 4) TESTS: Add hermetic pytest tests asserting: (a) _verify_before_push with uv absent from PATH returns a failure naming uv, and does not raise; (b) a resolver run in that state records a failure, makes no commit and no push, and the review loop halts with the error instead of proceeding to the next iteration; (c) a resolver container that exits non-zero halts the loop; (d) a final iteration with two approvals and one CHANGES_REQUESTED carrying one nit renders as 2/3 with that nit listed; (e) a Dockerfile test asserts that holon-base installs a pinned uv and runs the uv --version smoke check. 5) CONSTRAINTS: Australian English; no behaviour change apart from the above; no new Python dependencies; tests strictly via 'uv run pytest'; 'uv run task lint' and 'uv run task lint-docs' pass; respect the per-module line budgets of the flow package and do not raise any budget; keep all paths target-native; keep exactly the three append-only ledgers; merging stays with the human maintainer.
rationale: On a recent flow run the resolver crashed in two consecutive review iterations because uv was missing from its container. Both rounds of fixes were silently discarded. The loop carried on as though they had been applied, and the posted consensus claimed a unanimous approval with zero nits while one reviewer still requested changes. Whether a resolver can push currently depends on whether the agent happens to install uv. Shipping uv, failing loudly when verification cannot run, and reporting the true final verdict remove a silent data-loss path and a misleading review signal from every future flow.
acceptance_criteria: Every image built from holon-base has a pinned uv on PATH for the holon user, and the build fails if 'uv --version' does not run.

goal: Compute and report Dual Actual EV in Stage 5 calibration: Intrinsic/Clean EV (without pre-existing/pipeline bugs) and Observed EV (with bugs included), plus Bug EV Drag.
description:
When a flow execution encounters a pre-existing engine bug from a previous PR or an intermediate Stage 4 review/pipeline failure before converging to a clean, approved PR, Stage 5 calibration currently reports only a single Actual EV (and overwrites the Stage 3 E-... summary row with any REV-... summary row sharing the same plan_branch, treating status == 'halted_for_human' or an earlier failed REV-... row as p_success = 0.0). Update Stage 5 calibration so that two Actual EV metrics are computed and reported side by side:

1. Create a focused helper module `apps/sandbox-executor/src/sandbox_executor/calibration_ev.py` (< 200 lines) containing the dual-EV ledger scanning, computation, and markdown rendering helpers so that `apps/sandbox-executor/src/sandbox_executor/calibration.py` (currently >1,000 lines) has a net line delta <= 0 and zero new `# noqa` suppressions.

2. In `calibration_ev.py` and `calibration.py`:
   - Extend `ActualMetrics` with `ev_clean: float = 0.0`, `ev_with_bugs: float = 0.0`, `p_success_clean: float = 0.0`, `p_success_with_bugs: float = 0.0`, `impact_clean: float = 0.0`, `impact_with_bugs: float = 0.0`, and `bug_ev_drag: float = 0.0` (while keeping `actual.ev = actual.ev_clean` and `actual.p_success = actual.p_success_clean` for backward compatibility).
   - Extend `CalibrationDeltas` with `delta_ev_clean: float = 0.0`, `delta_ev_with_bugs: float = 0.0`, and `bug_ev_drag: float = 0.0` (with `deltas.delta_ev = deltas.delta_ev_clean`).
   - When scanning `executions.jsonl` summary records (`entry_type == 'summary'`) for a given `execution_id` and `plan_branch`:
     * **Clean / Intrinsic EV (`ev_clean`)**: Evaluate the final converged outcome (`E-...` execution summary and latest `REV-...` review summary). Treat `status in ('success', 'halted_for_human')` with `exit_code == 0` as a converged success (`p_success_clean = 1.0`, `impact_clean = predicted.impact`), computing `ev_clean = round((impact_clean * p_success_clean) - cost_effort, 2)`. Only if the final converged outcome itself failed (`status == 'failed'` or `exit_code != 0` with no subsequent converged recovery) is `p_success_clean = 0.0`.
     * **Observed EV (`ev_with_bugs`)**: Inspect all summary rows (`E-...` and `REV-...`) matching the `execution_id` or `plan_branch`. If any intermediate or earlier summary row recorded `status == 'failed'` or a non-zero `exit_code` (indicating a bug or pipeline failure was encountered during the run), `p_success_with_bugs = 0.0`, `impact_with_bugs = 0.0`, and `ev_with_bugs = round(0.0 - cost_effort, 2)`. When no failure rows exist across the run, `p_success_with_bugs == p_success_clean`, `impact_with_bugs == impact_clean`, and `ev_with_bugs == ev_clean`.
     * **Bug EV Drag (`bug_ev_drag`)**: Compute `bug_ev_drag = round(ev_clean - ev_with_bugs, 2)`.

3. In the calibration Markdown report (`format_markdown_report` / `calibration_ev.py` and `report_data` dictionary in `generate_calibration`):
   - Render both **Expected Value — Clean (without bugs)** and **Expected Value — Observed (with bugs included)** in the Executive Calibration Summary table and Mathematical Derivations section, along with **Bug EV Drag (`bug_ev_drag`)**.
   - To keep `calibration.py` net line count <= 0, move the markdown formatting helper or EV derivation block into `calibration_ev.py` and import it in `calibration.py`.

4. Add comprehensive unit tests in a new dedicated test file `apps/sandbox-executor/tests/test_calibration_dual_ev.py` verifying:
   - Clean runs (`status == 'success'` and `status == 'halted_for_human'` with no prior failed summary rows) produce `ev_clean == ev_with_bugs` and `bug_ev_drag == 0.0`.
   - Runs that hit an intermediate failed `REV-...` or `E-...` summary row before converging to `success` or `halted_for_human` produce positive `ev_clean`, negative `ev_with_bugs` (`-cost_effort`), and positive `bug_ev_drag == round(ev_clean - ev_with_bugs, 2)`.
   - Both EV rows and the bug drag annotation are rendered in `format_markdown_report()`.

Naming main as the target is legitimate: it selects the repository and the base branch. The flow must then run in a new worktree branched off main, and never mutate the main worktree.
goal: 1) REDIRECT: In cli/commands/flow.py and git_flow.py, when the resolved target worktree is an attached working tree whose checked-out branch is the intent's target branch (normally main), provision or attach the derived flow-<slug> sibling worktree using the existing derive_worktree_layout() and ensure_worktree() helpers, branched off origin/<target_branch>, and use it as the target worktree for every stage, for the checkpoint and for the run summary. Log the redirect at info level. A target worktree on any other branch is still used as it is, and the existing auto-provisioning of bare or absent targets is unchanged. 2) NEVER MUTATE: No stage may check out a branch in, commit to, or write ledger or calibration files into the default-branch worktree. 3) CHECKPOINTS: A new checkpoint records the provisioned flow worktree. Resuming from a checkpoint whose recorded target_worktree is a default-branch worktree fails fast, before any stage runs, with an actionable error that names the flow-<slug> worktree to use instead. 4) DIRECT ENTRY POINTS: holon review, holon review-loop and holon calibrate, which write to the working tree of the branch they run on, refuse to run when the target worktree has the default branch checked out, with an actionable error. 5) DOCS: Update the --target-worktree help text and the flow documentation to say that naming main selects the repository and base branch only, and that the run happens in a dedicated flow-<slug> worktree. 6) TESTS: Add hermetic pytest tests, using fixture repositories, asserting: (a) a flow targeting the main worktree is redirected to flow-<slug> branched off origin/main and all stages use it; (b) after the run the main worktree's HEAD, branch and git status are unchanged; (c) an already-existing flow-<slug> worktree is reused; (d) a target on a non-default branch is used as it is; (e) a checkpoint recording a default-branch worktree is refused with the actionable error; (f) holon review, review-loop and calibrate refuse a default-branch worktree. 7) CONSTRAINTS: Australian English; no new dependencies; tests strictly via 'uv run pytest'; 'uv run task lint' and 'uv run task lint-docs' pass; respect the per-module line budgets of the flow package and do not raise any budget; keep all paths target-native; keep exactly the three append-only ledgers; merging stays with the human maintainer.

description: When the Stage 4 resolver agent commits its edits locally inside the container, _commit_and_push_resolution captures initial_head after the commit and finds no uncommitted working-tree changes. It skips verification, git trailer creation, and git push, while flow.py mistakenly logs that a new head was pushed. At the next iteration git checkout wipes out the unpushed local commit, losing all fixes. Soft-reset any local resolver commits back to pre_resolver_head before verification and push, explicitly instruct the resolver not to run git commit or git push, and check the pushed flag in flow.py before logging.
goal: 1) CAPTURE PRE-RESOLVER HEAD: In sandbox_executor.entrypoint.review_loop (_run_resolver_mode), record pre_resolver_head before _run_resolver_agent executes, and pass it to _commit_and_push_resolution. 2) SOFT-RESET LOCAL RESOLVER COMMITS: In _commit_and_push_resolution, if current HEAD differs from pre_resolver_head, run 'git reset --soft pre_resolver_head' so all changes authored by the resolver agent are restored to the index/working tree relative to pre_resolver_head. 3) PROMPT INSTRUCTION: Update _build_resolver_prompt to explicitly state: 'Do not run git commit or git push yourself; leave your edits in the working tree so the harness can verify, attach review trailers, commit, and push.' 4) HONEST PUSH CHECK IN FLOW: In sandbox_executor.flow.review.loop (and wherever resolver outcome is processed), verify that resolver_outcome.pushed is True before logging 'Resolver pushed new head ...' and advancing the review target to the new head. 5) TESTS: Add hermetic pytest unit tests in apps/sandbox-executor/tests/test_review_loop.py asserting: (a) when _run_resolver_agent creates a local git commit during its turn, _commit_and_push_resolution soft-resets to pre_resolver_head, runs verification (_verify_before_push), re-commits with canonical Review-Iteration git trailers, and pushes HEAD:refs/heads/<head_branch> with pushed=True; (b) _build_resolver_prompt forbids both git commit and git push; (c) flow review loop requires pushed=True before treating the head as changed and proceeding to re-review. 6) CONSTRAINTS: Australian English; no behaviour change apart from the above; no new Python dependencies; tests strictly via 'uv run pytest'; 'uv run task lint' and 'uv run task lint-docs' pass; respect the per-module line budgets of the flow package and do not raise any budget; keep all paths target-native; keep exactly the three append-only ledgers; merging stays with the human maintainer.
rationale: Because the resolver prompt previously only forbade git push, resolver agents frequently ran git add and git commit before outputting dispositions.json. description: When a plan is decomposed into sub-intents, each child flow opens its pull request against the parent intent branch, not main. Every CI workflow restricts its pull_request trigger to branches: [main], so such pull requests get no checks at all. The Stage 4 review loop then finds no recorded test result and no CI checks, waits 180 seconds for checks to register and halts with 'test results not measured', even when all reviewers approve. Decomposed flows therefore cannot complete. Run the CI workflows for pull requests into any base branch so stacked sub-intent pull requests are tested like any other.
goal: 1) WORKFLOW TRIGGERS: In .github/workflows/, remove the 'branches: [main]' restriction from the pull_request trigger of docker-build.yml, make.yml, test-hygiene.yml, test-integration.yml, test-stress.yml and test-unit.yml so that pull requests into any base branch run them. Keep the push trigger limited to main, keep the existing pull_request types, the concurrency settings and workflow_dispatch, and do not introduce a configuration that runs the same checks twice for one commit. Leave build-images.yml (manual dispatch only) alone. 2) DOCS: Update .github/workflows/README.md and any CI notes under docs/ to state that pull requests into any branch run the checks and why (stacked sub-intent pull requests target their parent intent branch). 3) GUARD TEST: Add a hermetic pytest that reads every workflow file in .github/workflows/ and fails when a workflow that triggers on pull_request restricts it to named base branches, so the filter cannot return. Use only the standard library or a parser already in the project's dependencies; add no new dependency. 4) REVIEW LOOP ON STACKED PRS: Check the Stage 4 code that resolves CI checks and mergeability for a pull request (flow/github/ci.py, flow/github/pr.py and the review loop). If anything assumes the base branch is main, fix it so that a pull request whose base is a parent intent branch is handled like any other. Add a hermetic test for a stacked pull request whose base is an intent branch: checks are awaited and read, and results are recorded. 5) CONSTRAINTS: Australian English; no behaviour change outside CI triggers and the check resolution described above; no new dependencies; tests strictly via 'uv run pytest'; 'uv run task lint' and 'uv run task lint-docs' pass; respect the per-module line budgets of the flow package, and lower them if modules shrink; keep all paths target-native; keep exactly the three append-only ledgers; merging stays with the human maintainer.
rationale: Decomposition is the flow's answer to a plan that is too large for one pass, but its child pull requests are stacked on the parent intent branch and, with the current triggers, receive no CI. The review loop cannot then measure tests and refuses to declare consensus, so every sub-intent of every decomposed flow fails after the reviewers have approved the work. Running the existing checks on pull requests into any branch is the smallest change that lets stacked pull requests be tested and lets decomposed flows finish.
acceptance_criteria: The six CI workflows run for pull requests into any base branch, and still run on push to main only.
A pull request whose base is a parent intent branch receives the same checks as a pull request into main.
A pytest fails if a pull_request-triggered workflow restricts its base branches.
The Stage 4 check and mergeability resolution is covered by a test for a stacked pull request.
All tests pass via 'uv run pytest', and 'uv run task lint' and 'uv run task lint-docs' pass.

description: When a plan is over its entropy budget the flow splits it into sub-intents and runs each as a child flow, but the split is decided and recorded in the wrong place and the children are cut from the wrong branch. Stage 3's executor container re-decides the split and records the sub-intent list in an executions.jsonl summary row (status 'decomposed'); the engine reads the list from that row. Each child intent is cut from, and its pull request targets, the parent intent branch, a sibling of the parent plan. As a result the parent plan and the parent execution record are on a side branch that no child contains and that never reaches main, children do not build on each other because each is cut before the previous child's pull request has merged, no pull request from the integration branch to main is ever raised, and resuming a decomposed flow re-runs a child that already has an execution branch and pull request, opening a duplicate pull request and overwriting that child's checkpoint. Make the plan own the decision, make the execution only run the children, nest every child under the plan branch, and give decomposed flows a route to main.
goal: 1) THE PLAN RECORDS THE DECISION: After the planner writes the plan, the Stage 2 plan step records the decomposition decision on the plan's plans.jsonl row on the plan branch, using the single existing should_decompose rule that the flow already applies to the plan row and plan file before dispatching the executor: the decision (execute, decomposed or over_budget), the entropy and the entropy budget, and for a decomposed plan the machine-readable sub_intents list (slug, description and goal for each item). The plan branch is then self-describing. Update docs/ledger_schema.md for the new plans.jsonl fields. 2) THE EXECUTION ONLY EXECUTES: For a decomposed plan the Stage 3 executor container does not re-decide the split and does not write the sub-intent list into its summary row. The execution runs the sub-intents recorded on the plan, strictly one after another, and its summary row refers to the plan's recorded decision and to the children (slug, intent branch, execution branch, pull request). The executor container and the flow must apply one rule, read from the plan row, never two. 3) CHILDREN NEST UNDER AND TARGET THE PLAN BRANCH: Each child intent is created from the plan branch (I-.../P-.../_), its branch name nests under the plan (keep the deterministic parent-plus-index-plus-slug naming), its recorded target_branch and parent_intent_id are the plan branch, and its pull request targets the plan branch, never the parent intent branch and never main. The parent plan file and the parent plan row are therefore ancestors of every child branch. 4) THE FLOW MERGES CHILD PULL REQUESTS INTO THE PLAN BRANCH: After a child's Stage 4 consensus review and Stage 5 calibration, with the calibration report already merged into the child pull request, the flow engine merges that pull request into the plan branch with a merge commit (not squash and not rebase, so the child's commits stay ancestors of the plan branch). It does so only when CI is green and the pull request is mergeable, and it first brings the plan branch's latest state into the child if needed, resolving ledger-only conflicts by interleaving rows on created_at. The engine must refuse to merge any pull request whose base branch is main or another default branch, and must have a test proving that refusal. Child N plus 1 is cut from the plan branch only after child N has merged, so children build on each other. 5) A COMBINED PULL REQUEST REACHES MAIN: When every child has merged into the plan branch, the flow raises the integration pull request into the intent's target branch, runs the review loop and calibration on the combined diff, includes the calibration report, and stops at the human merge boundary. That pull request must carry the parent plan, the parent execution record and the plans and execution records of every child. Choose the head branch (the plan branch, or the execution branch updated from it) so this is true, keeping children merging into the plan branch. The flow summary lists every child pull request and the combined pull request. 6) RESUME SAFETY: A resumed decomposed flow continues an existing child at the stage where it stopped, using that child's own checkpoint, execution branch and pull request. It never re-dispatches a child that already has an execution branch or an open or merged pull request, never opens a duplicate pull request, and never overwrites a child's checkpoint with a new run. Record child progress in the parent checkpoint so a resume knows which children are done, in progress or pending. 7) DOCS: Update docs/architecture.md and docs/git_flow.md so they describe this behaviour and no longer describe the interim behaviour of cutting children from and targeting the parent intent branch. 8) TESTS: Add hermetic pytest tests with fixture repositories asserting: (a) the plan row carries the decision and the sub_intents list and the executor does not write its own; (b) every child branch has the parent plan branch tip as an ancestor and its pull request base is the plan branch; (c) child N plus 1 is cut after child N merged and contains its changes; (d) the engine merges a child pull request into the plan branch with a merge commit and refuses a pull request whose base is main; (e) the combined pull request is raised, carries the parent plan, the parent execution record and all child plans, and stops for the human; (f) resuming after a child's review failed continues that child, opens no duplicate pull request and leaves the other children's checkpoints intact; (g) a plan within budget is unaffected. 9) CONSTRAINTS: Australian English; no new dependencies; tests strictly via 'uv run pytest'; 'uv run task lint' and 'uv run task lint-docs' pass; respect the per-module line budgets of the flow package and do not raise any budget without a recorded reason; keep all paths target-native; keep exactly the three append-only ledgers; the combined pull request into main is merged only by the human maintainer.
rationale: A decomposed flow is the flow's answer to work that is too big for one pass, but today it cannot finish. The first decomposed run split into four children, cut each from the intent branch where the parent plan is not an ancestor, ran child one's review, then on resume re-ran child one from scratch and opened a duplicate pull request. The parent plan that explains the split would never reach main, later children would be written blind to earlier ones, and no pull request would carry the combined work into main. The decision belongs to the plan, which is the deciding node; the execution should only run the children, each nested under and merged into the plan branch, with a single combined pull request for the maintainer.
acceptance_criteria: The plan row on the plan branch records the decomposition decision and sub_intents list, and the executor container no longer decides or writes the split.
Every child branch descends from the parent plan branch, and every child pull request targets the plan branch.
The flow merges a child pull request into the plan branch with a merge commit after consensus and calibration, and refuses to merge any pull request whose base is main.

A combined pull request from the plan branch into the target branch is raised after the last child, carries the parent plan, the parent execution record and every child plan, and stops for the human maintainer.
Resuming a decomposed flow continues an existing child, opens no duplicate pull request and keeps each child's checkpoint.
