description: Sandbox role containers (the Stage 4 review ensemble and resolver, and the stage executors) currently work in named Docker volumes and run 'git reset --hard HEAD', 'git clean -fdx', 'git fetch origin' and 'git checkout -B <branch> origin/<branch>' on every launch. A container that crashes, times out or is killed loses every unpushed edit and local commit on the next launch, and cloning inside a sandbox needs GitHub egress, a token and a ready proxy sidecar. Named volumes are root-owned, need a root chown init container, and leave orphans. Replace this with a clean division of responsibilities: the host provisions and bind-mounts a dedicated git worktree, and the container works directly in it with no cloning, no destructive reset and no volume machinery.
goal: 1) HOST PROVISIONS AND MOUNTS: Before starting a role container, the host validates that the target worktree is an existing, attached git worktree (provisioning the dedicated sibling flow-<slug> worktree off origin/main through the existing worktree helpers when it is absent) and bind-mounts it into the container at /home/holon/.holon-sandbox/workspace. Make the worktree's backing git directory resolvable inside the container (for example by mounting the repository's git directory at the path the worktree's .git file points to, or by another hermetic mechanism) so git commands inside the container work without network access. Dispatch the container without creating named Docker volumes and without a root chown init container. 2) CONTAINER WORKS IN PLACE: The container finds the workspace already provisioned and performs no git clone, no git fetch to prepare the checkout and no destructive wipe. It validates that the workspace exists, reads git rev-parse HEAD, then runs the role directly on the mounted worktree. The review ensemble, the resolver and the executors keep running their edits, linters and test suites in the mounted workspace, and continue to create canonical-trailer commits and push directly (git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<branch>), so the host does not intermediate commits or pushes. Files written by a container are immediately present on the host, so a crash, OOM or timeout loses nothing. 3) UNIFIED INTERMEDIATE ARTIFACTS: All intermediate subagent files (reviewer turn prompts, agent responses, dispositions JSON, stderr tails, scratch notes and review state) are written under <worktree>/.subagent/ (singular, already git-ignored), for example <worktree>/.subagent/review/iter-<N>/, so that manual host-side review skills and the containerised review loop read, write, resume and audit the same location. 4) WORKTREE NAMING AND REUSE: The flow-<slug> worktree is the single persistent worktree for all five stages: opening a pull request never renames, deletes or recreates it, and calibration, resumed runs (--checkpoint, --from-stage) and re-triggered reviews reuse it. pr<N>-<slug> is only used by standalone review commands when no local worktree exists for that branch, and must never be created when a flow-<slug> worktree is already checked out for it. Concurrent ensemble reviewer turns that need their own test runs use ephemeral sibling worktrees named flow-<slug>-rev<index>, pruned automatically when the iteration completes. 5) PURGE OBSOLETE CODE AND TESTS: Delete, rather than deprecate or leave behind a fallback, all in-container git and volume machinery that this makes obsolete: in entrypoint/review_loop.py the _clone_or_fetch, _reset_reused_checkout, _ensure_head, _origin_matches and _has_checkout functions and every caller, simplifying workspace initialisation to the validation in point 2; in flow/review/workspace.py the Docker named-volume creation (docker volume create), the root chown init container, volume teardown and pruning heuristics, review_session_volume_name and the HOLON_REVIEW_PERSIST handling; and any related code in agent_runner.py and cli/commands/flow.py. Search the whole target repository, including docs and CI configuration, for remaining references and remove or update them. Delete the unit tests that assert named volume creation, root chown, container-side cloning or reset behaviour. 6) NEW TESTS: Add hermetic pytest tests asserting: (a) the host worktree is validated or provisioned and bind-mounted into the container with its git directory resolvable; (b) the container starts with no remote clone, fetch or destructive reset; (c) files written by the container appear immediately on the host worktree; (d) a simulated container crash preserves uncommitted edits and test logs on the host; (e) intermediate artifacts land under <worktree>/.subagent/; (f) no named volume is created and no root chown container is launched; (g) an existing flow-<slug> worktree is reused, never replaced by a pr<N>-<slug> worktree. 7) CONSTRAINTS: Australian English; no new dependencies; tests strictly via 'uv run pytest'; 'uv run task lint' and 'uv run task lint-docs' pass; respect the per-module line budgets of the flow package and do not raise any budget (the purge should lower them); keep all paths target-native; keep exactly the three append-only ledgers; merging stays with the human maintainer.
rationale: In-container git plumbing is fragile and has already lost work: a resolver's unpushed local commits were wiped by the destructive preamble on the next iteration. Cloning inside a sandbox also ties every launch to GitHub egress, a token and proxy readiness, and named volumes add root-owned directories, an init container and orphaned state to clean up. Mounting a host-provisioned worktree gives every role the same hermetic workspace, makes crashes lossless, keeps manual and containerised reviews in one shared location, and lets a large amount of defensive code and its tests be deleted. Removing the old paths entirely matters: leftover duplicate code paths would mislead future readers into thinking in-container cloning is still supported and would keep legacy tests that mask real regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Role containers work directly in a bind-mounted host worktree: no git clone, no fetch to prepare the checkout, no git reset --hard or git clean -fdx, no named Docker volume and no root chown init container.
A simulated container crash or timeout leaves all uncommitted edits and test logs on the host worktree.
Intermediate review artifacts are written under the worktree's .subagent/ directory.
An existing flow-<slug> worktree is reused across stages and resumes, and a pr<N>-<slug> worktree is never created for a branch that already has one.
The obsolete in-container git functions, volume machinery and their tests are deleted, with no remaining references in code, docs or CI configuration.
All tests pass via 'uv run pytest', and 'uv run task lint' and 'uv run task lint-docs' pass, with the flow module budgets lowered, not raised.

description: The Stage 4 review loop can declare consensus, post a review headed 'APPROVED (3/3)', halt for the human and run calibration while a reviewer's critical finding is still open. On a recent run the reviewer container's own summary read 'Ensemble: CHANGES_REQUESTED', with reviewer 3 at CHANGES_REQUESTED (critical 1) and the Security role at CHANGES, yet the host loop logged 'Consensus approval reached', and the posted review listed reviewer 3 as APPROVED with zero findings while its own role table still showed Security as CHANGES. The change was merged on the strength of that review and later reverted because the open critical finding was a real sandbox escape. The host decides consensus with 'if ensemble_verdict is ConsensusVerdict.APPROVED' in flow/review/loop.py. The likely cause, not yet confirmed, is that findings the resolver had already adjudicated are filtered out before the verdict is computed: the resolver had rejected many findings as 'out of scope', including important ones, so a critical raised again was probably dropped as already adjudicated and the reviewer's verdict flipped to approved. The same shape of premature consensus (a reviewer still at CHANGES_REQUESTED) has been seen on earlier runs. Make the consensus decision depend only on what the reviewers actually returned, and make the posted review report it exactly.
goal: 1) FIND AND FIX THE CAUSE: Reproduce the behaviour first with a hermetic test shaped like the failing run: three reviewers returning APPROVED, APPROVED and CHANGES_REQUESTED with one critical finding, where an earlier iteration holds a resolver row that rejected a finding with the same identifier or text as 'out of scope'. Determine from the code (flow/review/loop.py, flow/review/resolver.py including _filter_adjudicated_findings, flow/review/records.py, review_ensemble.py, review_report.py) exactly where the reviewer's verdict changes between the reviewer's returned result and the verdict the loop acts on, and fix that cause. Document the cause in the pull request description and in the code comments of the fix. 2) CRITICAL AND SECURITY FINDINGS ARE NEVER SUPPRESSED: Adjudication suppression (handing earlier rejected findings to later reviewers as already adjudicated, and filtering them from a later verdict) applies to Nit findings only. A critical finding, an important finding, or any finding raised by the Security role is never filtered from the verdict, whatever an earlier resolver row says. A finding raised again at a higher severity than the one it was rejected at is a new finding. 3) THE VERDICT COMES FROM WHAT THE REVIEWERS RETURNED: The ensemble verdict is computed from each reviewer's returned verdict and counts. If a reviewer returned CHANGES_REQUESTED, or any role verdict is CHANGES, the loop does not declare consensus, does not post an approving review and does not halt for the human as approved; it proceeds to the resolver. If any pre-filter and post-filter verdicts differ, log both with the finding identifiers and do not declare consensus. 4) HONEST POSTED REVIEW: The posted consensus review lists every reviewer's verdict and finding counts exactly as returned, and its headline fraction counts only reviewers who returned APPROVED with zero open findings. It must never be headed APPROVED while any reviewer or role is CHANGES. Add a test that renders a review for the failing shape and asserts it is not an approval. 5) RESOLVER REJECTIONS NEED EVIDENCE: A resolver rejection of an important or higher finding must carry a specific, evidenced reason naming the code it checked (file and line or test), and 'out of scope' alone is not accepted for important or higher findings: such a finding is recorded as still open and goes to the next iteration as open. Add tests. 6) FLOW-END WORDING: Any end-of-flow message, summary line or notification must report the final ensemble's verdicts and say plainly when any reviewer's final verdict was not APPROVED, and must not describe such a run as ready for merge. 7) DOCS AND LEDGER: Update docs/git_flow.md and docs/ledger_schema.md for the adjudication rule (nits only) and the verdict rule. Keep exactly the three append-only ledgers. 8) CONSTRAINTS: Australian English; no new dependencies; tests strictly via 'uv run pytest'; 'uv run task lint' and 'uv run task lint-docs' pass; respect the per-module line budgets of the flow package and record a reason for any raised budget; keep all paths target-native; merging stays with the human maintainer.
rationale: A review that says approved while a critical finding is open is worse than no review: it removes the one human check that depends on the review being true. A real sandbox escape reached main this way and had to be reverted. The loop's decision and its posted record must come from what the reviewers actually said, and a rejection by the resolver must never be able to silence a later, more serious report of the same problem.
acceptance_criteria: A test reproducing three reviewers at APPROVED, APPROVED and CHANGES_REQUESTED (critical 1) with an earlier 'rejected: out of scope' row for the same finding yields no consensus, no approving post and a proceed-to-resolver outcome.
Adjudication suppression applies to Nit findings only; critical, important and Security-role findings are never filtered from the verdict.
The posted review lists each reviewer's verdict and counts exactly as returned and is never headed APPROVED while any reviewer or role is CHANGES.
A resolver rejection of an important or higher finding without an evidenced reason leaves the finding open.
End-of-flow messages state the final ensemble verdicts and never describe a non-approved run as ready to merge.
All tests pass via 'uv run pytest', and 'uv run task lint' and 'uv run task lint-docs' pass.

description: A decomposed flow builds branch names that exceed GitHub's limit on a full ref name, and the failure stops the whole flow. A child branch nests the parent plan branch, the child slug, its own plan and its execution branch, and every plan and execution segment carries the agent and model labels (for example 'claude-agent-claude-sonnet-5-5'). In a recent run the child execution branch was 282 characters (293 with the 'refs/heads/' prefix). GitHub rejected the push with 'remote: ref too long' and 'pre-receive hook declined', the executor exited with code 1, and the work survived only as a printed 'UNPUSHED EXECUTION PATCH'. The limit was measured against the real service: a full ref name of 255 characters, counting the 'refs/heads/' prefix, is accepted and 256 is rejected, so a branch name without the prefix can be at most 244 characters. The calibration branch adds the suffix '/calibrated' in place of '/_', 9 characters more. Nothing in the engine measures a name before it creates it.
goal: 1) ONE LIMIT, ONE BUILDER: Define a single documented constant for the maximum full ref length (255, counting 'refs/heads/') and route every branch name the engine creates through one function that checks it: the root intent branch, plan branch, execution branch, the calibration branch (which uses the suffix '/calibrated' instead of '/_', so every name is checked as if it ended in '/calibrated'), and every decomposed child intent, plan and execution branch at any depth. A name that fits is left exactly as it is today, so no existing branch, checkpoint or ledger row changes. 2) DETERMINISTIC SHORTENING: When a name would exceed the limit, shorten only the segments the engine controls, in this order: the child slug, then the agent and model labels inside nested plan and execution segments, then the root intent slug, replacing the cut part with a stable 6-character hexadecimal digest of the original text so two different long inputs never collide. Shortening is deterministic (the same input always gives the same name), keeps the timestamp and the 8-character identifiers intact, and the original unshortened slug and labels are recorded in the intent, plan and execution ledger rows. A resumed flow keeps the names it already created and never recomputes them. 3) EARLY AND NAMED FAILURE: If a name cannot be made to fit even after shortening, Stage 1 fails before any branch is created, with a message naming the limit, the computed length and the segment that cannot be shortened. A rejected push caused by ref length, if it ever still happens, is reported by name ('ref too long', the branch and its length) rather than as an executor exit code, and the unpushed work is not discarded. 4) TESTS (hermetic, no network): the real failing case (the 56-character slug with four sub-intents and the claude-agent / claude-sonnet-5-5 labels) now builds names that are at most 255 characters with the prefix and 255 with '/calibrated'; boundary tests at names of 243, 244 and 245 characters without the prefix and at 254, 255 and 256 with it (a name that fits is unchanged, the first over the limit is shortened); determinism; no collision between two long slugs that share a prefix; depth three children; a resumed flow keeps its existing names; the ledger rows record the original text; an impossible name fails at Stage 1. 5) DOCS: describe the limit, its measured value and the shortening rules in docs/git_flow.md. 6) CONSTRAINTS: Australian English; no new dependencies; tests strictly via 'uv run pytest'; 'uv run task lint' and 'uv run task lint-docs' pass; respect the per-module line budgets of the flow package and record a reason for any raised budget; keep all paths target-native; keep exactly the three append-only ledgers; merging stays with the human maintainer.
rationale: A flow that decomposes is the flow's answer to work that is too large, and today the largest work is the work most likely to fail on a branch name after the agent has finished its job. The limit is a fact about the service, so the engine should know it, measure every name against it, and shorten deterministically instead of failing at the last step.
acceptance_criteria: Every branch name the engine creates is checked against one documented limit of 255 characters including the 'refs/heads/' prefix, and checked as if it ended in '/calibrated'.
A name that fits is unchanged; a longer name is shortened deterministically with a stable digest, and the original text is recorded in the ledger rows.
